newsitem.title: INDIA: India says divestment depends on market conditions.
newsitem.headline: India says divestment depends on market conditions.

text.p: Indian Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Wednesday that market conditions would determine the timing of the sale of partial stakes in state-controlled firms.
"It depends upon the market conditions," Maran told Reuters when asked when the government would begin the first round of divestment in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31.
"We have to wait and see," he said.

The government has set a target of raising 50 billion rupees in 1996/97 from divestment, or the sale of partial stakes in state-controlled firms. Last year India raised 3.57 billion rupees from divestment, well short of the target of 70 billion.

India has planned to sell a seven percent stake in telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and five percent in crude oil refining company Indian Oil Corp in the first round of divestment in 1996/97.
But the government has not able to fix a date for kicking off the first round of divestment.
"We cannot sell our crown jewels just for a song," Maran said, speaking on the margins of a meeting of the heads of state-owned companies. "We have to wait for a better price."
Maran urged the chiefs of state firms to suggest ways to improve profitability and efficiency.

He said loss-making state firms were a burden on the government budget. There are 241 state firms, out of which about 130 firms make a total profit of 120 billion rupees while 109 firms make a loss of 50 billion, he added.
"The United Front government will help the public sector units to make them strong and competitive," Maran said, referring to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left coalition.
